opening_message:
Ticket 1: Traci Lowe (employee ID E041) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E041.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin on Source Code. Admin requires the Engineer role; as a non-owner, max is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Traci Lowe (E041) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Traci Lowe (E041) requested admin on Source Code. Admin requires the Engineer role (owned by Engineer) — Traci is an Analyst per HR, so admin is not permitted under either note. Additionally, the Security DB lists Traci as a contractor with basic security training, which caps access at read (write requires advanced training; admin is never allowed for contractors). Because the two notes conflict on employment type (full_time vs contractor), I grant the most restrictive maximum that is valid under both interpretations: read.
